correctness.rationale: Exact arc-block counting: a proper h-arc subset of a fixed directed k-cycle is a disjoint directed path union and occurs in a uniform order with probability 1/(n)_h; the entire k-cycle occurs with probability zero. Two inclusion-exclusion steps prove the exact finite expectation. For finitely many vertex-disjoint cycles of total L arcs, counting feasible single-color arc assignments gives n^{-L} times the product of (r^{k_i}-r), with O(n^{-L-1}) duplicates from multiple-colored arcs. Distinct cycles sharing a vertex have more edges than vertices in their union; their bounded embedding sums contribute O(n^{-1}). Thus all joint factorial moments converge to those of independent Poisson variables. The extracted exact-rational checker exhaustively agrees for (n,r)=(2,1),(3,2),(4,2),(4,3) and all k<=n, with success marker ALL_EXACT_CYCLE_CHECKS_PASS. All special cases, including k=2, k=n and r=1, are covered by the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary work concerns finite-model decidability for independent successor relations, not random sampling or mixed directed-cycle counts. The other 2026 successor paper concerns satisfiability certificates. The 2015 Hamilton-path union paper studies extremal families, not a joint Poisson profile for uniform independent paths. Random permutation and random regular graph cycle laws are analogous but their model permits cycles in individual colors or has different sampling; they do not directly imply the exact -(r/k) correction. The already-known r=2,k=2 opposite-successor coincidence law is subsumed as only one special case and is not claimed as a stand-alone discovery. No accessible exact table, matching formula, or stronger covering theorem was located; historical priority remains subject to the stated access risk.
residual_risks: A specialized Poisson small-cycle or conditioned-permutation theorem for superposed directed Hamiltonian paths, if it exists, could imply the new result.
Frieze (2001) full text was inaccessible; abstract inspection cannot rule out a stronger relevant result.

value.rationale: The exact short-cycle profile addresses a natural logical statistic on finite structures with several invisible linear-order successors. Its joint distribution yields a complete limiting law for every finite list of short directed-cycle predicates and gives the entire directed-girth distribution, including sharp nonzero/nonone sentence probabilities. The intensity correction r/k persists at every fixed length, distinguishing path superposition from sparse independent arcs and making global per-color acyclicity locally observable after forgetting colors. The exact finite expectation is natural and reproducible rather than an arbitrary small case; no downstream paper-size consequence is required.
